question: Does a controller improved through component acquisition and contract-aware compatibility transfer to useful chronological appliance-energy forecasting?

data.creator: Luis Candanedo
data.scope: Raw dataset download only; no forecasting or test outcome computed.

method: Controllers fixed fromP63/P65; no application-based choice. Inputs are past/current appliance Wh transformed by training-only log1p median/std and tanh. Runtimes remain unchanged. Fit three linear forecast readouts on first60percent; lock before validation/test. Validation20percent never changes settings. Test last20percent; horizons10min,1h,4h, exclude targets crossing partition boundaries; state carried causally. Same source-label exposure and ridge for all neural models and64-lag ridge AR; persistence and daily-seasonal references. No room/weather covariates used.
primary: P65 contract controller vs P63 accepted runtime: >=1percent lower1hour test RMSE, paired144-sample block-bootstrap95percent interval for improvement above0, and no more than1percent degradation at other horizons. Stronger operational competitiveness vsAR64/persistence/seasonal is reported separately. Report all five runtimes and three classical baselines even if primary fails.
costs: Carry P63/P64/P65 development and pool preparation as inherited research work. Report application readout fitting, native inference/compiled-port work, wall/memory and unchanged controller hashes separately. All neural controllers get equal source forecast labels; none of their pretrained weights or execution parameters changes. No measured electricity or savings claim.
scope: Single low-energy-house public measurement series at10min resolution. Forecast transfer on one variable, not an entire industrial deployment or state-of-the-art multivariate comparison. Source model arrays and program contracts were acquired on a different synthetic numerical workload.
stopping: One chronological split and fixed source-derived scaling/forecasters/hyperparameters. No tuning or controller selection against validation/test. Preserve all results and errors; engineering failures require recorded new version.
